chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Ayyub, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): We wish to hasten the departure, and it was the Night of Departure when I asked him, so at what time should we depart? He said to me, 'As for the second day, do not depart until the sun sets, and it was the Night of Departure.'
As for the third day, when the sun has brightened (risen fully), then depart in accordance with the Book of Allah, for indeed Allah, Exalted and Glorious, says:
So whoever hastens [his departure] in two days - there is no blame upon him; and whoever delays - there is no blame upon him.
If he had remained silent [and only mentioned hastening], no one would remain but those who hasten, but he said, 'And whoever delays - there is no blame upon him.'

key_terms.ابْيَضَّتِ الشَّمْسُ: The sun brightens/rises fully (indicating the time for the third day's departure)
key_terms.تَزُولَ الشَّمْسُ: The sun sets (specifically referring to the time for Maghrib prayer)
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ النَّفْرِ: Night of Departure (referring to the night of the 11th or 12th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific times for leaving Mina on the 2nd and 3rd days of Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between the second and third days of Tashreeq, emphasizing that while haste is permissible on the second day, the third day requires departure after sunrise to avoid the generalization of 'hastening' that might lead to early departure. By explicitly quoting the phrase 'and whoever delays, there is no blame upon him,' the Imam prevents the community from assuming that only hastening is virtuous, thereby preserving the balance between speed and deliberation in the ritual of leaving Mina. This narration highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise timing (waqt) as a means of adhering strictly to the divine text while avoiding the pitfalls of literalist interpretation.
